This entry is NOT validated against current published research — treat every mechanism and claimed efficacy [ESTIMATE] claim as unverified legacy material until full v2 enhancement lands. \n\nTARP extends conventional tool‑use prompting by introducing a recursive planning loop. The model first generates a high‑level task graph describing required subtasks. Each subtask is evaluated for whether it should be solved internally (reasoning) or externally (tool execution). When a tool is required (e.g., Python interpreter, search engine, database query, simulator), the model generates a tool call specification and executes it. The results are fed back into the planning loop where the model reassesses the global objective and continues decomposition. This recursive loop continues until all nodes of the task graph are resolved.
